newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to offer management rights for oil plant.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to offer management rights for oil plant.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament voted on Friday to hold a tender for rights to manage the state's stake in the country's second-largest oil refinery, Lisichansknaftorsyntez.
Parliamentary speaker Alexander Moroz said the tender for the 75.3 percent government stake would be open to Ukrainian firms with no more than 25 percent foreign investment.
Ukraine fears foreign investment in its six refineries, particularly from neighbouring Russia, which supplies oil to its neighbour.
The tender winner would have to pay off the Lisichansk refinery's debts, guarantee to refine no less than 6.5 million tonnes of oil a year and upgrade the facility.
The government announced last year it planned to offer a 45 percent stake in the plant to a strategic foreign or domestic investor. It was not clear how the management tender might affect that plan.
Refinery workers own 24.7 percent of the refinery.
Government statistics show Lisichansk owed 108 million European currency units to an unnamed German bank and had other debts of 136 million hryvnias.

The refinery, built in 1976, processed 2.16 million tonnes of oil in 1996 compared to 2.31 million tonnes in 1995. In 1990, just before independence from the Soviet Union, it refined 21.8 million tonnes.
Ukraine's oil refineries are capable of processing 60 million tonnes annually but refine far less than that.
